building.amendments_note: Article II amends the IBC only for a new residential Group R-X (Sections 302.1, 310.6, 429, 903.2.8), Chapter 4 operating features, Section 1010.2.12, Chapters 13, 27, 31, 32 and 33 and Appendix D. fixtures.basis: Alabama has no statewide code for private commercial buildings, so Birmingham's Technical Code decides for offices and restaurants. It adopts the 2021 International Plumbing Code with no change to Chapter 4, the same edition and table the State Building Code uses for schools, hotels and state buildings. So the city's counts equal the state pack's worked examples, and they are restated here as Birmingham's own. The table and sections were read on UpCodes' copy of the unamended 2021 IPC (secondary), which the state pack also used.

office.quote: Business: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 | 1 per 75

table_rows.split_rounding_quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
table_rows.urinal_quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
table_rows.separate_rooms_quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.
table_rows.stall_quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. [...] Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 1 each. Urinals: up to 50% of 1, so none.
100 each. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: 67% of 1, so none.
50 each. 50/75 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25/50 rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: none.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Same figures as the Alabama state pack (same 2021 table). K-12 schools fall under the State Building Code, which uses the same table. The urinal limit applies 'in each bathroom or toilet room'; the figures assume one men's room holds all the men's fixtures.

occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Business areas | 150 gross ... Educational | Classroom area | 20 net

Any owner, authorized agent, or contractor who desires to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a building or structure [...] shall first make application to the Building and/or Fire Official and obtain the required permit for the work. EXCEPTION: Permits shall not be required for the following work except as noted herein: 1. Any portable heating, ventilation, evaporator coil or cooling equipment. [...] 4. Repair or replacement of components with similar equipment which does not enlarge, move, convert, or replace the mechanical system and which does not create an unsafe condition. [...] 10. Repair of commercial roofing including gutters and downspouts, if repair does not include changing the type of roof material. [...] 12. Painting, papering, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops, and similar finish work in single family residences. [...] 14. Playground equipment. 15. Ordinary minor repairs may be made with the approval of the Building, Code, and Fire Official without a permit, provided that such repairs shall not violate any of the provisions of this Code.
permit.note: The 15-item list was read in full. Item 15 drops the model code's 'partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches'; item 12 (finish work) is limited to single family residences. Toilet partitions are not named. The city's Building Permit brochure adds: 'All commercial construction work regardless of size of the project requires a building permit as per the Technical Code of the City of Birmingham.' Neither text says whether swapping toilet partitions counts as construction work, an alteration or an ordinary minor repair.

restrooms_city.note: No city ordinance or code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found. The Technical Code doesn't amend the plumbing code's Chapter 4, so the 2021 model rules apply in the city as adopted: single-user rooms identified as available to all persons regardless of sex (403.1.2) and a shared room allowed where each toilet is in a compartment and urinals are in stalls or visually separated (403.2 exception 6). Birmingham's non-discrimination ordinance (No. 17-121) covers gender identity in public accommodations but has no restroom provision (text searched for restroom, bathroom, toilet, locker, shower). The Birmingham City Code on Municode was not searched (blocks automated access).
restrooms_city.quote: Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex. [2021 IPC 403.1.2, UpCodes copy]

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Birmingham job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Alabama humidity and see the city rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Birmingham offices, hospitals, schools and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Birmingham's building rules, like Alabama's state rules, require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Birmingham sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Birmingham access rules:** the list of rules Birmingham reviews plans against also names a national accessibility standard, in its 2017 edition.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Birmingham's plumbing rules, as under the state's, a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone, and a shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. Alabama law requires shared restrooms in public K-12 schools and public colleges to be designated for one sex.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Birmingham requires a permit to alter or repair a building, and the city's permit guide says all commercial construction work needs one, whatever the size of the project. The list of work that needs no permit covers "nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, and counters" and doesn't name toilet partitions. Ordinary minor repairs may be made without a permit if the city's building official approves. Ask the Department of Planning, Engineering and Permits (205-254-2211) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: Birmingham's Department of Planning, Engineering and Permits
page.stalls_intro: Alabama's state building rules cover schools, hotels, movie theaters and state-funded buildings. For other buildings, such as private offices and restaurants, Birmingham's own rules decide. Both use the same table, so the counts match. Birmingham counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to two thirds of the toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen. The table shows men's toilets as stalls.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office designed for 25 people or fewer, a shop designed for 100 or fewer, and any building designed for 15 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. Confirm the count with Birmingham's Department of Planning, Engineering and Permits.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Birmingham's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Department of Planning, Engineering and Permits sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors on permitted building work in Birmingham pay city license fees set by ordinance. Alabama requires a state general contractor license for commercial jobs of $100,000 or more. Birmingham's permit guide still gives $50,000, the figure before the state raised it, as the point where a state-licensed general contractor must take out the permit, so confirm what your project needs with the Department of Planning, Engineering and Permits. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor on a commercial job of $100,000 or more in Alabama needs a state general contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Alabama has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work. For a carpenter on building work in Jefferson County that is $18.43 an hour, with no separate benefits amount.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 10% in Birmingham: 4% state, 2% Jefferson County and 4% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, clinics and university buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, with accessible stalls in every room.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (adopted by Alabama in place of ICC A117.1 within the State Building Code); ICC/ANSI A117.1-2017 (listed on Birmingham's Building Plans Review Sheet); Technical Code of the City of Birmingham, 2024 (effective October 1, 2024): 2021 International Building Code as amended in Article II, 2021 International Existing Building Code, 2021 International Plumbing Code and 2021 International Fire Code, with the city's own Chapter 1 (Section 103.1.1 for work exempt from permits); Alabama State Building Code: 2021 International Building Code with Alabama exceptions and 2021 International Plumbing Code (schools, hotels, movie theaters, state-owned or state-funded buildings); NFPA 286 for HDPE (International Building Code Section 803.9).
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a Birmingham building permit, or counts as an ordinary minor repair under Section 103.1.3 (Planning, Engineering and Permits, 205-254-2211; pre-construction meetings 205-254-2224).

Birmingham's Technical Code (Section 103.4.1) and its Building Permit brochure still give $50,000 as the commercial job size above which the contractor must hold a state general contractor license; the state threshold has been $100,000 since October 1, 2024 and the code says 'or as same may be amended'. Ask the department which figure its counter applies.

The ordinance number and adoption date of the 2024 Technical Code were not found (a June 18, 2024 council agenda listing it is no longer online); the city's Building Codes page gives the effective date, October 1, 2024.
The city's Building Permit brochure still lists the 2015 code editions; the Technical Code and the plan review sheet say 2021. The page follows the Technical Code.

The 2021 model code text (toilet table, floor area per person, the HDPE fire-test section, single-user restroom signs) was read on UpCodes, not on ICC's site: check once in a browser at codes.iccsafe.org.

The fire-test section says 'used as an interior finish'; the 2021 definition of interior finish names toilet room privacy partitions. Whether Birmingham's plan reviewers ask for the test report on toilet partitions was not confirmed.
What ICC A117.1-2017 changes for stalls compared with the federal standard was not read; the access bullet only says the city lists it.
The local contractor rule's source link is the Municode copy of the city code, which blocks automated access; the same text (Section 103.5) is in the Technical Code PDF cited in Sources.
The federal carpenter rate for Jefferson County ($18.43, no fringe) is a 2017 survey rate, below the area's median carpenter wage on the page ($24.23); both figures are as published.
Sales tax: an out-of-state seller in Alabama's simplified program collects a flat 8%, not Birmingham's 10%; which applies to Next Partitions is a question for Abe's accountant.
